nodes.label: Orchestration Layer

nodes.label: Guardrail Layer

nodes.label: Kaiju GAIS (substrate)
nodes.desc: The self-healing, self-documenting substrate Daikaiju AIOps runs on -- not a separate product. Four layers: self-healing, memory, onboarding, naming.

nodes.desc: Detection on the pi-node: the acting watchdog runs every 5 minutes and a Docker-events trigger starts it about 45 s after a monitored container dies, is removed, runs out of memory or goes unhealthy.

nodes.label: STEP 2: Known-Fix Triage
nodes.desc: Checks whether a detected issue matches a known FM-01...FM-07 pattern. Same underlying FASHSD logic as Step 1 -- peels into the same detail.

nodes.label: STEP 3: Escalate & Brief
nodes.desc: Mokaima pulls vault context and writes a brief for Bakaidah, following the MABS standard. The entry point whenever FASHSD can't auto-resolve something.

nodes.label: STEP 4: Bakaidah Reasoning
nodes.desc: Bakaidah Daikaiju (gemma4-bakaidah:31b via Open WebUI, A2A server on :<port>) drafts a proposed fix. Runs its own self-chain, reliability filters, and a parallel Kaiju Relay verification pipeline.

nodes.label: STEP 5: Mokaima Review
nodes.desc: Mokaima checks Bakaidah's proposed fix before anything gets executed. Approve -> Angkai executes it. Reject -> flagged for manual review, pipeline stops here.

nodes.label: STEP 6: Angkai Execution
nodes.desc: Angkai (Claude Code on dokaisho, via Qwen/Ollama) actually runs the approved fix. Self-chains its own output and is checked by the Stop hook validator.

nodes.label: STEP 7: Resolution Check
nodes.desc: A mechanical check suite verifies the execution actually worked. Passes -> resolved. Fails -> retry loop back to Angkai, or escalate back to Mokaima/Bakaidah for a different approach.

nodes.label: 21 individual MABS rules
nodes.desc: See P4 for every rule individually.

nodes.label: Citation Grounding Filter
nodes.desc: An Open WebUI Pipe that intercepts Bakaidah's response and forces every factual claim to carry a real citation back to a source document, rather than letting Bakaidah state things unsupported.

nodes.label: Diagnostic History Filter
nodes.desc: An inlet Filter that injects relevant Troubleshooting_Journal.md history into Bakaidah's context before it answers, so it reasons with awareness of past incidents instead of starting cold each time.

nodes.label: Enforcement Gate Filter
nodes.desc: An inlet Filter that checks incoming requests against Bakaidah's hard rules (MABS, install-path prohibitions) before generation even starts, catching violations at the door rather than after the fact.

nodes.label: Incident Fabrication Filter
nodes.desc: A Filter built specifically to catch Bakaidah inventing incidents that never happened -- built after Bakaidah was caught fabricating incident numbers/details in a real response.

nodes.label: MABS Few-Shot Filter
nodes.desc: An inlet Filter that injects real few-shot examples of correct MABS-compliant briefs into context, so Bakaidah has concrete examples to pattern-match against, not just abstract rules.

nodes.label: MABS Topic Match Filter
nodes.desc: A Filter that detects when the current task is MABS-relevant (writing a brief for Angkai) and activates the MABS-specific guardrails only when actually needed, rather than always.

nodes.label: Reference Existence Filter
nodes.desc: A Filter (, v0.5) that checks every file/path Bakaidah references in a REFERENCES section against the real filesystem before letting the response through -- catches fabricated file paths.

nodes.label: Structured Brief Drafter Filter
nodes.desc: A Pipe that structures Bakaidah's output into the MABS brief format directly, rather than relying on Bakaidah to freehand the structure correctly every time.

nodes.label: Skill: citation-grounding
nodes.desc: An Open WebUI Skill (attached document) that teaches Bakaidah citation-grounding conventions -- loaded into context, not code that runs.

nodes.label: Skill: existence-verification-escalation
nodes.desc: An Open WebUI Skill teaching the existence-verification-escalation pattern -- when a single failed search isn't enough to conclude something doesn't exist, and what tiers of checking to escalate through instead.

nodes.label: Skill: references-verification
nodes.desc: An Open WebUI Skill teaching Bakaidah how to properly verify and format REFERENCES sections before claiming a file exists.

nodes.label: Kaiju Relay Design Doc
nodes.desc: The design document for Kaiju Relay -- the architectural reasoning behind why an isolated-context 3-stage pipeline exists separately from Bakaidah's own Filters/Pipes.

nodes.label: Model Relay (Stage A/B/C)

nodes.label: Checkpoint Gate

nodes.label: Brief ID Collision Check
nodes.desc: A mechanical check that catches brief-ID collisions -- two different tasks accidentally reusing the same tracking ID, which would corrupt cross-referencing.

nodes.label: Update Preservation Check

nodes.label: update_preservation_check.py

nodes.label: Rule 1: Length ceiling (~200 lines)
nodes.desc: Caps how long a single execution brief can be, forcing Mokaima to split large tasks into multiple smaller briefs rather than one sprawling brief Angkai is more likely to misread or lose context from.

nodes.label: Rule 2: Embed everything, never make Angkai discover
nodes.desc: Every fact, path, or value Angkai needs must be written directly into the brief -- Angkai should never have to search vault or infer something on its own, since that's where drift and misreadings happen.

nodes.label: Rule 3: One output per phase
nodes.desc: Each phase of a brief produces exactly one deliverable, not several bundled together, so Angkai's own pause-and-report cycle stays clean and Mokaima can verify one thing at a time.

nodes.label: Rule 4: MCP paths use vault/ prefix
nodes.desc: All filesystem paths in a brief must use the vault/ prefix Angkai's MCP tools expect, not an OS-absolute path -- a real bug came from paths not matching this convention.

nodes.label: Rule 5: Minimize MCP reads during execution
nodes.desc: Briefs should embed what Angkai needs rather than relying on it to read multiple files live during execution, since every extra MCP call is a chance to hit a tool bug or drift from what Mokaima verified.

nodes.label: Rule 6: Hard prohibitions block
nodes.desc: A fixed list of actions Angkai is never allowed to take (installing outside /srv, touching boot/EFI/swap without explicit approval) -- these override anything else in a brief, no exceptions.

nodes.label: Rule 7: Pause points between every phase
nodes.desc: Angkai must stop and wait for explicit confirmation after each phase rather than running a whole multi-step brief unattended end to end.

nodes.label: Rule 8: One script per brief
nodes.desc: A single execution script per brief, not several -- keeps what Angkai is running traceable to one clear source rather than a chain of separate files.

nodes.label: Rule 9: Tell Angkai how to end
nodes.desc: Every brief must explicitly state what a successful finish looks like, so Angkai isn't left guessing whether it's actually done or should keep going.

nodes.label: Rule 10: Reference scripts go inline
nodes.desc: Any script Angkai needs to run gets pasted directly into the brief rather than referenced by path, removing a step where Angkai could read the wrong version or fail to find it.

nodes.label: Rule 11: Sequence steps explicitly
nodes.desc: Steps must be numbered and ordered explicitly in the brief, not left for Angkai to infer a reasonable order from a looser description.

nodes.label: Rule 12: Specify exact command per section
nodes.desc: Each section of a brief states the literal command to run, not a description of what should happen -- removes room for Angkai to improvise the wrong command.

nodes.label: Rule 13: State permissions negatively
nodes.desc: Permissions are written as what's NOT allowed rather than what is, since an explicit prohibition list is harder to accidentally violate than a vague 'use good judgment' positive framing.

nodes.label: Rule 14: Verify filesystem pre-reqs + shared-resource deps
nodes.desc: Before Angkai starts, the brief must confirm the files/directories it depends on actually exist and that no other process is using the same resource -- traces directly to real FASHSD live-test incidents.

nodes.label: Rule 15: Never cross-reference two tables
nodes.desc: A brief should never make Angkai look something up in one table then cross-reference it against a second table -- that kind of indirection is exactly where real mistakes happened.

nodes.label: Rule 16: Paste full current file when extending
nodes.desc: When a brief asks Angkai to extend an existing file, it must paste that file's full current content, not just a diff or summary, so Angkai works from the real current state, not a stale assumption.

nodes.label: Rule 17: Name every expected file, forbid others
nodes.desc: Every file the brief expects Angkai to create or modify must be named explicitly, and creating anything else is forbidden -- the rule the Stop hook validator mechanically checks.

nodes.label: Rule 18: Strengthen pause points, phase-per-message
nodes.desc: A stronger version of Rule 7 -- pauses should be structural (Angkai literally cannot proceed without a new message), not just instructional text asking it to wait.

nodes.label: Rule 19: REFERENCES manifest block
nodes.desc: Every brief must include a REFERENCES section listing every file path it relies on, which the Stop hook validator spot-checks for real existence.

nodes.label: Rule 20: Classify brief type before writing
nodes.desc: Before writing a brief, Mokaima must first classify what type it is (build, fix, investigate, etc.), since different types call for different structure and level of caution.

nodes.label: Rule 21: Pre-write verification
nodes.desc: Before rewriting or substituting any existing content, first confirm the write target actually matches what the task asked for, and re-read the file fresh rather than trusting a cached earlier-session copy -- built after a real incident where a stale assumption caused an overwrite.
